meta.title: Shivam Sharma — Full Stack Developer · Engineer of Interfaces & Systems
meta.description: Shivam Sharma — Full Stack Developer building polished frontend experiences and reliable backend systems across enterprise workflows.

profile.heroHeadline: Writing interfaces in React and reliable backends in Node — four years across enterprise workflows, three sectors, one practice.
profile.heroSummary: I started writing software with a fixation on interface — the place a person actually meets the product. That work, four years of it across enterprise products in healthcare, community operations, and lending, taught me how a real application is shaped: where data lives, how state is invalidated, why latency is felt before it's measured. Frontend was never the surface; it was always the system, viewed from a particular angle.
profile.availability: Open to frontend, backend, and full-stack engineering opportunities.

education.degree: Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering
education.school: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow

projects.title: WellCare Health
projects.description: A multi-tenant healthcare platform that reinforced service-heavy application design, secure access models, and API-driven workflows across patients and providers.

projects.title: TheSwapp

projects.title: Node.js API Foundations
projects.description: A personal full-stack transition project focused on building RESTful APIs with Node.js and Express.js. It was designed to strengthen CRUD flow handling, middleware structure, routing clarity, and modular server-side organization while preparing for MongoDB-backed APIs.
features: Built RESTful endpoints with clear routing and modular server-side structure.
Implemented CRUD operations and organized request / response flow cleanly.
Used middleware for request handling, validation flow, and reusable backend logic.
Structured the project as a practical backend fundamentals exercise while moving from frontend into full-stack work.
projects.note: Personal backend practice project created to represent real learning progress, not fabricated corporate backend experience.
